content_preview.title: Firefox 157 Ships Nova Redesign, Compact Mode and Hardware AV1 Decoding for WebRTC Calls
content_preview.summary: Mozilla's Firefox 157 brings the Nova visual refresh, a returning compact mode, hardware AV1 decoding in WebRTC, and new CSS support for at-rule() and overscroll-behavior: chain.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Mozilla released Firefox 157 to Release channel users on September 29, 2026, according to its [release notes](https://www.firefox.com/en-US/firefox/157.0/releasenotes/). The headline change is what Mozilla calls the "biggest visual refresh in years," a modernized look across the browser's toolbars, sidebar, menus and individual features. [Phoronix](https://www.phoronix.com/news/Firefox-157-Released) refers to the redesign as the Nova UI and notes the release arrives as part of Mozil...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured Briefing (608 words, inside the 300-800 range): Overview, interface changes, media and web platform, privacy/search, and a candid 'What We Don't Know' section. Neutral tone, no AI self-reference, no editorializing.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three snapshots from disk (gunzip, HTML to text); all returned HTTP 200 with no archive fallback and suspicious_patterns is null for all three, so no injection text to evaluate. source-0.html.gz (firefox.com Firefox 157.0 release notes): confirmed verbatim 'Version 157.0, first offered to Release channel users on September 29, 2026'; 'Firefox's biggest visual refresh in years ... modernized look across the browser toolbars, sidebar, menus and individual features' (article's quoted 'biggest visual refresh in years' is verbatim); 'A new compact mode that reduces toolbar and tab spacing to leave more room for web content, useful on smaller screens and in split-screen layouts'; 'WebRTC video calls can now use hardware AV1 decoding on devices that support it, instead of always decoding AV1 video in software' (no OS, GPU or platform list is given; the article states exactly 'on devices that support it' in the body and says in What We Don't Know that qualifying devices are not listed); the three fixes (sideways/upside-down WebRTC video, 8-bit HDR dull/gray on Windows, A/V sync when changing playback speed); the encryption-key-logging warning; Firefox Suggest country list (16 countries, matches); Amazon removal with custom-engine fallback; Tab focus change; updated sidebar enabled for everyone, sidebar.revamp=false in about:config also turns off vertical tabs, preference available until end of 2027, 'Show sidebar' removed from Settings; alert/confirm/prompt dialogs, color and date pickers and autocomplete follow page light/dark scheme; at-rule() in @supports with the @supports at-rule(@scope) example; chain value for overscroll-behavior; 21 brand new volunteers. source-1.html.gz (Phoronix, Michael Larabel): confirmed 'Nova UI' as 'the biggest visual refresh in years', 'bi-weekly release regiment', hardware AV1 decode for WebRTC 'on supported devices', and 'Up to now Firefox was always relying on software decoding for AV1 videos with WebRTC'. Note: Phoronix is dated 28 September 2026 (binaries on the FTP) while Mozilla's notes say first offered 29 September; the article uses Mozilla's date and attributes it to the release notes, which is correct. 'Nova' appears only in Phoronix (and in gHacks reader comments about browser.nova.enabled), not in Mozilla's notes; the article correctly attributes the term to Phoronix. source-2.html.gz (gHacks, Arthur Kay, Sep 30 2026): confirmed Compact Mode 'is back after requests from users who wanted more room for web content', 'Mozilla added an auto compact option for smaller screens', new theme picker with built in themes in light and dark versions plus new wallpapers, and the release-notes reference for split screen. Allowlist: firefox.com is not on config/source_allowlist.txt (triggering the automated warning) but is Mozilla's own first-party release-notes site; ghacks.net is also not on the allowlist, is a long-running tech news outlet used here only for corroboration plus interface details (auto compact, wallpapers, 'back' framing) that I verified in the snapshot. Treated as an allowlist gap, not a reputability problem; firefox.com, developer.mozilla.org and firefox-admin-docs.mozilla.org added to the allowlist as first-party Mozilla documentation, ghacks.net deliberately left off.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Headline-qualifier check (the Firefox 156 'up to 45%' pattern): no numeric or comparative claim is overstated. The headline 'Hardware AV1 Decoding for WebRTC Calls' omits 'on devices that support it', but this is a capability claim that the body states with the exact Mozilla qualifier twice (Media section and What We Don't Know); the headline does not assert universal availability, so I treat this as acceptable headline compression, not a correctable overstatement. 'Nova' in the headline is Phoronix's name for the redesign, attributed to Phoronix in the body; Mozilla's own notes do not use the word. 'Compact mode' is described by Mozilla as 'new' and by gHacks as 'back'; the summary's 'returning compact mode' follows gHacks and the body attributes each framing separately. No default-on/opt-in status for compact mode is stated in any source and the article does not claim one; the updated sidebar default-on status ('now enabled for everyone') is correctly stated. The 'no performance measurements' statement in What We Don't Know is accurate (gHacks quotes Mozilla's 'no cost to your browser performance' marketing line, which is not a measurement and is not repeated). Release date Sept 29, 2026 matches Mozilla. No fabricated specifics or invented quotes; every body URL is in article.sources.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; claims are attributed to Mozilla, Phoronix or gHacks.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. The sister Firefox 156 article (2026-09/30) covers a different release; no other Firefox 157 coverage exists in the archive.
concerns: Headline and summary drop the 'on devices that support it' qualifier on hardware AV1 decoding; mitigated because the body states it explicitly and the headline makes no universal claim.
firefox.com and ghacks.net are not on the source allowlist (automated warning only).
recommendations: Preserve the 'on supported devices' qualifier in headlines and summaries for hardware-dependent features.
firefox.com, developer.mozilla.org and firefox-admin-docs.mozilla.org added to config/source_allowlist.txt as first-party Mozilla documentation.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced, correctly qualified release-notes briefing. The only automated warning is an allowlist gap for Mozilla's own first-party site, so APPROVE without corrections.
